name: Mapping Helper Single and 10x
concept: A white cursor steps ~3 px/s along the strip, leaving dim ten-pixel blocks in a 5-colour cycle behind it so an installer can count pixel indices.
visual_verdict: Almost entirely black: a single dim red/green/blue block plus one white dot crawling along the first row of the grid; nothing to look at.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the spec (explicit repaint instead of framebuffer persistence), but the idea is a mapping tool, not content.
action_notes: Pixel-identification is a job for the web UI's mapper/identify feature, not a library pattern; if kept anywhere it belongs in a tools/diagnostics set alongside the other mapping helpers, never the shipped library.

name: marching rainbow (buffered)
concept: Broad rainbow bands march one way while a fine fast ripple carves moving dark notches through them the other way; framed as a 'buffer in beforeRender' teaching demo.
visual_verdict: Busy horizontal rainbow streaks with lots of black; on a grid it is just a 1D strip smeared into row stripes, noisy rather than pretty.
perf_smell: 2x array(pixelCount) recomputed every frame with 3 nested wave() per pixel in an interpreted loop (32 KB of buffers at 4096 px)
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec exactly; the spec itself is the same visual as marching-rainbow with a 0.12 vs 0.2 phase nudge, existing only to teach buffering.
action_notes: Same look as marching-rainbow (which already has march-time/ripple/depth/mirror controls); delete this file and keep the buffering lesson in docs/lang.md where fillHSV is documented.

name: marching rainbow
concept: Rainbow bands march along the strip with a counter-moving fine ripple chopping them into beating bright/dark segments; hue warped by a triple-nested wave.
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows diagonal rainbow-flecked slashes on black, half the strip dark at all times; lively but chaotic and harsh, gaudy hue flicker inside each band.
perf_smell: 4 wave() per pixel (3 nested for hue) — cheap but could be one fillGradient-style pass
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the spec; the spec's idea (difference of two waves, nested-wave hue) is thin and the hard negative clip makes it look choppy.
action_notes: Absorb marching-rainbow-buffered; soften the clip (smoothstep the difference instead of hard clamp), reduce hue flicker by dropping one nesting level, and consider OKLCH so the bands do not dip in blue. Could be one mode of a consolidated 'Rainbow' pattern if the rainbow family is collapsed.

name: Marquee Chase
concept: Theater-marquee chase: blocks of lit 'bulbs' in a picked colour march along the strip, unlit bulbs keep a faint filament glow.
visual_verdict: Clean orange/black diagonal stripes in the waterfall — a smooth scroll of 5 blocks; legible but flat, and on the grid it is just row stripes.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: BUG: sliderBlocks declares min=1 max=10 real units but still rescales with 1 + floor(x*9.99), so the UI default 5 gives 50 blocks. Rewrite as a real marquee: discrete bulbs (every Nth pixel) stepping in theater-chase steps with filament warm-up/cool-down easing and an incandescent warm tint, which is what makes a marquee look real; drop the 'UI controls tour' framing.

name: matrix 2D honeycomb
concept: Sin+cos plasma whose spatial scale breathes, folded through a triangle and cubed so it reads as thin glowing neon contour rings drifting and morphing.
visual_verdict: Neon contour lines (green/cyan/yellow/blue rings and X-crossings) on black that reshape frame to frame; genuinely nice, though hue range stays in a narrow green-blue band most of the time.
perf_smell: sin+cos+triangle per pixel; fine (could separate x and y terms into row/column tables in renderBulk)
cleanroom_quality: Port correctly fixed the hardcoded 8-wide serpentine decode into a real render2D; the name 'honeycomb' is misleading — there is no hexagonal structure.
action_notes: Same sin+cos breathing-zoom plasma as sinpulse-3d, only folded through triangle and cubed into neon contour lines. Make that fold a 'neon contours' style of the consolidated Plasma (sinpulse-3d survivor) with a hue-spread control so it travels the whole wheel; drop the misleading 'honeycomb' name. Precompute sin(x*f)/cos(y*f) per column/row in beforeRender.

name: matrix 2D pulse edit
concept: A dim index-driven plasma whose pseudo-coordinates come from index/3 and index mod a fractional animated zoom, producing breathing aliased stripes.
visual_verdict: Nearly black: faint teal/green dashes and dot lattices on most frames, two frames essentially empty; looks like a broken mapping, not a design.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithfully reproduces the original's accidental bugs (row divisor 3 vs width 8, fractional modulo) — exactly the pixel-fidelity trap the overhaul rejects; the idea underneath is just the honeycomb plasma.
action_notes: The 'edit' is a buggy derivative of matrix-2d-honeycomb's plasma; nothing worth absorbing beyond what honeycomb already does.

name: Matrix 2 tone pulse
concept: Interference plasma locked to two complementary hues that never blend — every transition fades through black — with a breathing zoom.
technique: per-pixel hsv math on index (deliberate aliasing)
visual_verdict: Dark purple speckle/aliasing moire on the grid; the yellow-green primary tone barely shows at all (cubing crushes the low half), so it reads as one dim violet noise field.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Keeps the index-mod-fractional aliasing and the hardcoded width on purpose; the genuinely good idea (two complementary tones separated by black seams) is lost because the cube makes the primary half invisible.
action_notes: Make 'two complementary tones separated by black seams' a palette style (with a hue picker) of the consolidated Plasma (sinpulse-3d) on real render2D coordinates; drop the index aliasing and zigzag toggle entirely.

name: Matrix Green Waterfall 1D
concept: Strip reading of digital rain: a few independent drops with near-white heads and squared green tails, each with its own speed, glyph-flicker dropouts in the tail.
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows clean green diagonal streaks at varied slopes with bright heads — reads well on a strip; on the grid it only lights the first rows.
perf_smell: array(pixelCount) zeroed and rebuilt every frame in an interpreted loop; renderBulk fade()+setPixel per drop head would need no buffer
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Make one 'Digital Rain' that runs on strips (this drop model) and grids (per-column drops) from the same renderBulk core: fade(k) for tails, setPixel(gridIndex(col,row)) or setPixel(i) for heads, hue control in degrees. Keep this file's real-unit controls (drops, px/s, trail px).

name: Matrix Green Waterfall 2D
concept: Stateless digital rain: each column is a floored-mod ramp of (y - phase) by a column length taken from a wave of x, squared, heads slightly bleached.
visual_verdict: Dense green vertical bars of varied length; columns sit in smooth arch/comb shapes because cycle length varies smoothly with x, so it reads as a sweeping bar-graph rather than independent rain; heads barely whiter than tails.
perf_smell: none (cheap closed form)
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec; the spec's own stateless trick gives an obviously periodic, smoothly-varying column structure that undermines the random-rain illusion. Speed slider is a bare 0..1 dial.
action_notes: Fold into the single Digital Rain; at most keep its 'stateless, cheap background layer' as a low-cost mode, using hash(col) for cycle lengths instead of wave(x) so columns are independent.

name: matrix rain
concept: Single cool-hued dots (green-cyan to blue) fall down random columns of a hardcoded 32x8 logical grid, fading toward the bottom.
visual_verdict: Sparse lone 1x4 dashes in cyan/blue scattered on black, most of the panel dark, no trails — very weak.
perf_smell: render2D per pixel only to light ~10 dots; renderBulk clear()+fillRect per drop would be near-free
cleanroom_quality: Faithful (including the hardcoded 32x8 logical grid that letterboxes oddly onto a square panel); the idea is a minimal trail-less rain and adds nothing over digital-rain-2d.
action_notes: Its only distinguishing feature (per-drop cool hue variety) can be a 'hue spread' control on the merged Digital Rain.

name: Metaballs of Fire 2D
concept: A few bouncing control points whose distance product forms a metaball field; blobs bulge, fuse and split, lit with a dim molten red-amber ramp.
technique: per-pixel distance field over N points
visual_verdict: Fused amber-orange blobs with red rims on black, clearly metaball-like and organic; but dim, low-contrast and more 'lava lamp' than fire — no flicker, no white-hot core.
perf_smell: dist() (sqrt) per pixel per point (5-8 sqrt/px) — slowest pattern so far at 0.45 ms; motion frame-rate dependent
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the product-of-distances metaball trick faithfully, but keeps the frame-rate-dependent motion and bare 0..1 sliders; the 'fire' part is weak.
action_notes: Keep the fusing-blob idea but compute the field on a small canvas (e.g. 32x32, squared distances, no sqrt) and upscale with fillCanvas/paintCanvas, or use classic 1/r^2 sums; add a proper fire palette (black-red-orange-yellow-white) with a noise flicker on the rim, dt-based motion, real-unit controls (blob count step=1, speed in px/s). Consider absorbing fireblobs/sound-lavablob as palette/sound modes.

name: Meteor Shower
concept: Fast meteors with pastel white-hot heads and tails that dim while gaining saturation, written into a rotating HSV ring buffer; hues drift slowly and successive meteors are colour neighbours.
visual_verdict: Dense parallel coloured streaks with bright heads fading through vivid colour to black; lively on a strip but meteors are almost back-to-back so it reads as scrolling stripes rather than discrete meteors.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount) ring buffers (48 KB at 4096 px) read per pixel
cleanroom_quality: Faithful and well controlled (real-unit speed/tail/gap/hue-cycle); the saturation-growing tail is the nice touch worth keeping.
action_notes: Best of the strip comet family; make it the survivor for comets/rainbow-comet/bulk-comet-trails. Optionally rebuild as renderBulk with a meteor list + per-meteor tail drawn by fillRange gradient (no 3 full-length buffers), raise default gap so meteors read as individuals, and add a 2D mode (diagonal streaks via drawLine + fade) for panels.

name: MidpointDisplacement1D
concept: A midpoint-displacement fractal mountain range as brightness along the strip, with a slice of the hue wheel scrolling through the height field; regenerates every few seconds.
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows rainbow chevrons rippling over a fixed terrain shape with dark ends; colourful but busy and the terrain shape is barely legible behind the hue scroll; regeneration is an instant cut.
perf_smell: none (generation is amortized)
cleanroom_quality: Correct algorithm with linear-interp sampling (improvement over per-pixel array), but all six controls are bare 0..1 dials (house-style violation) and the hard regeneration cut is jarring.
action_notes: Give controls real units (lifetime seconds, scroll Hz, hue offset/width in degrees, roughness as a Hurst-like factor); crossfade old to new terrain over ~1 s instead of cutting; optionally scroll the terrain itself (generate ahead and pan) so it reads as a flight over mountains. On 2D, draw it as a real filled skyline silhouette (height = column fill) — that would be the cool version.

name: millipede 1d/2d controls
concept: An actual millipede creature — plated segments with peristaltic bunching, metachronal leg wave, paler head with eyes and sweeping feelers — crawling a ring around the panel (or the strip loop in 1D).
visual_verdict: A clearly readable green segmented critter with bristling legs and a pale head crawling around a ring; charming and unique, though leg detail is noisy at 32x32 and colour is a single green.
perf_smell: atan2 + hypot + pow + several sin per pixel, all pixels shaded even though the creature covers ~15% of the panel — 0.70 ms, the heaviest in this range
cleanroom_quality: Explicitly forked from the original by Jeremy's 2026-09-01 brief; delivers a much better creature than the spec's abstract rainbow pinwheel.
action_notes: Rename to 'Millipede' and take over the slug once millipede.js is gone; move to renderBulk drawing segments as splats/drawLine capsules along a path (and let the path wander via a curl-noise or Lissajous track rather than a fixed ring) so cost scales with the body, not the panel. Fix 'controls' in the display name.

name: millipede
concept: Abstract rainbow cut into repeating half-spectrum segments crawling along the strip, with brightness ripples locked to the hue bands and a sinusoidal surge-and-stall gait.
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows dense diagonal rainbow comb-stripes with wavy drift — saturated and busy, reads as a generic rainbow ripple rather than anything leg-like.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful with sensible real-unit controls, but the 'millipede' idea only exists in the name; visually it is one more rainbow scroller.
action_notes: The name belongs to the creature (millipede-1d-2d-controls); this abstract rainbow crawl is redundant with the marching-rainbow/rainbow family. If any of it survives, the surge-and-stall gait could be a 'gait' toggle on the consolidated rainbow scroller.

name: multimap simpledemo
concept: Framework demo splitting one display into regions (centre disc, one quadrant), each running its own mini-pattern; first match wins.
technique: per-pixel region dispatch via function arrays
visual_verdict: A green top-left quadrant pulsing and a blue disc blinking in the centre on black — a placeholder demo, not content.
perf_smell: function-array dispatch per pixel per region
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: region layering is exactly what scenes (layers with masks/projection) do natively
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to a framework demo; the framework itself is superseded by Luxel scenes.
action_notes: Scenes already partition/compose a display; if a region-split example is wanted, ship a small example scene (pattern A in a disc, pattern B in a quadrant) in library/scenes instead.

name: Multisegment Demo
concept: Home-automation zone framework: up to 12 strip zones each with on/off, colour, brightness and one of 19 mini effects, driven by exported arrays or web-UI sliders, with a fade-in/out state machine.
visual_verdict: Four solid colour blocks (red, dim olive, cyan, dim violet) fading up from black; nothing moves by default.
perf_smell: 19-branch if-chain per pixel with time() calls inside render
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: zones are an engine/scene concern (segments/layers addressed by API), not pattern code
cleanroom_quality: Reproduces the framework, but all UI sliders are bare 0..1 dials and the per-zone UI is clunky (active-zone slider + shared latch); the actual automation contract is a third-party protocol.
action_notes: Propose an engine feature instead: strip segments/zones as first-class scene regions settable over the API (HA integration can then address segments). Remove from the shipped library.

name: Opening Act
concept: Music-choreography framework (beat/tempo/instrument detection + a beat-timed queue of mini-patterns) with an 8-look demo show: progress bars, beat sweeps, quarter/eighth strobes, bass oscilloscope, surge, pitch piano.
visual_verdict: On the grid the whole sheet is a red progress bar growing/blinking across columns — 1D content stretched over x; flat and mostly single-hue for the 8 s sampled.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount+1) scratch buffers allocated though the v2 renderers barely use them; closure call per pixel
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: a beat-timed sequence of looks is a scripted scene/playlist, not a pattern
cleanroom_quality: Thorough port of the framework with sensible real-unit controls; but the framework is a strict subset of the v3 'Main Stage' port and its looks are 1D only.
action_notes: Delete; any v2-only look (bass oscilloscope, pitch piano) moves into the v3 survivor's mini-pattern set. Sound-analysis code is duplicated verbatim-in-spirit across three files — see v3 note.

name: Main Stage
concept: Big music-VJ framework: audio analysis (volume AGC, kick/clap/hi-hat detectors, tempo estimation), a beat-measured queue and 15 mini-patterns (ocean, fizzle, build-up, surge, analyzer, elastic spring chain...) with a scripted loop show.
visual_verdict: Grid shows 1D textures wrapped row-by-row in wire order (noisy green/teal/red speckle bands) with long dark stretches waiting for sound; impossible to read as a show on a panel.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount+1) shared scratch (48 KB at 4096 px), plus the theme-hue add/subtract loop over the buffer
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: the sequencer half is a beat-synced scripted scene/playlist; the mini-patterns would each be better as standalone sound patterns
cleanroom_quality: Ambitious and functional port; the 'manual pattern' dial is a good fix. But everything is 1D index-space, so on a 2D panel it looks broken, and the 730-line file is unmaintainable library content.
action_notes: Propose an engine feature: beat/tempo detection as builtin sensor outputs (beatPhase, bpm, kick/clap/hat triggers) and beat-synced scene/playlist sequencing; then extract the best mini-patterns (elastic spring chain, fizzle, build-up, analyzer) as standalone sound patterns with 2D renderings, and ship the show itself as an example beat-scripted scene. Absorbs music-sequencer-for-v2 and flash-posterize-music-sequencer-framework.

name: Nano Orbital
concept: For Nanoleaf-style modular builds: one LED per 12-LED panel lit, all panels stepping in lockstep once per second, rainbow across the installation.
visual_verdict: Sparse single rainbow dots every 12 px marching in lockstep — thin dotted diagonals on the waterfall; looks like a test pattern on anything but the author's exact hardware.
perf_smell: array(pixelCount) cleared and rebuilt per frame just to mark 1 px in 12 (renderBulk clear()+setPixel loop needs no buffer)
cleanroom_quality: Correctly fixes the panelCount/pixelsPerPanel generalization bug, but pixelsPerPanel is an edit-the-source constant and the idea is installation-specific.
action_notes: Per-panel repetition is a mapping/tiling concern (scene projection or the tiling feature) rather than a pattern; nothing visually worth keeping.

name: NaturalLightSync
concept: Circadian lamp: one uniform white whose colour temperature follows a parabola from warm at sunrise/sunset to cool at solar noon, warmest overnight.
technique: clock + blackbody curve fit, uniform fill
visual_verdict: Solid uniform orange-white across all frames — correct for a circadian lamp (static by design).
perf_smell: per-pixel render of a single constant colour; renderBulk fill() would be one call
cleanroom_quality: Faithful, but leaves sunrise/sunset/temperature range as edit-the-source constants though the spec itself calls out exposing them as sliders.
action_notes: Make utilitycolortemp the single 'White Light' utility with a Kelvin dial plus a 'follow the day' toggle that runs this parabola (sunrise/sunset hours and min/max Kelvin as real-unit controls); render with renderBulk fill(). Also share the Kelvin-to-RGB fit with sunrise-alarm-clock.

name: neutronorbit
concept: An 'atom' on a strip: three warm comets oscillate sinusoidally, staggered by a third of a cycle with fading tails, around a throbbing white nucleus; per-channel max makes crossings flash white.
visual_verdict: On the grid it is index-space so just short red/orange/pink dashes in a few rows; on a strip three warm smears and a white blob — pleasant but low energy and a narrow warm palette.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount) trail buffers plus an interpreted setPixel loop over every pixel; the persistent frame + fade() already gives trails for free
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec, with good real-unit controls; the node-graph origin shows in a lot of machinery for a modest effect.
action_notes: Rebuild on renderBulk: fade(k) for tails, fillRange/splat humps for comets, no buffers. Give it a real 2D form — electrons on tilted elliptical orbits (splat mode 1) around a pulsing nucleus — which would be a genuine panel showcase; keep the strip form as the 1D projection.

name: Newfire
concept: 1D Doom-fire: a heat array fed from a constant source advects with random 1-2 cell jitter and cooling at a fixed 25 Hz tick, with sparks/sputters near the base and a white-hot core via saturation headroom; four layout modes (start, end, centre-out, both ends).
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows a convincing flickering orange-to-black flame from the base with streaky licks; a solid strip fire, though the white core is faint and the palette is plain orange.
perf_smell: interpreted per-cell advection loop with random() per cell (fine on strips; at 4096 px index-space it would be poor but it is a strip pattern)
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec well (fixed tick, modes, sputters); three of four sliders are bare 0..1 dials and the hsvPicker satHead*1.8 trick is opaque.
action_notes: Good candidate for the surviving 1D fire: absorb fire-red/fire-blue as palette presets (classic, blue gas, green, custom picker), give flame height in % of strip and spark rate in sparks/s, and use a black-red-orange-yellow-white palette via paint() rather than single-hue hsv so the core actually goes white.

name: novas
concept: Soft bursts bloom at random spots, pop on white-hot, widen and dim over seconds into crimson or orange-red tints; brightest wins on overlap.
visual_verdict: On the grid it is index-space, so blooms are horizontal pink/brown/white bars across rows; washed-out muddy browns and pinks, the slowest pattern in this range.
perf_smell: 4x array(pixelCount) (tmp + r/g/b) cleared and rebuilt per frame with interpreted per-pixel loops — 0.75 ms at 1024 px
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the machine-generated original (two identical generators) with decent controls; the result is muddy because tint+white lerp then squared produces browns.
action_notes: novas, portal and scrolls are the same machine-generated 'pulse pool summed into a field, mapped through a palette' design. Make portal the single 'Blooms' pattern with palette presets (embers = this file's white-hot-to-crimson, fire portal, bioluminescent), pulse interval/lifetime/spread controls, implemented on renderBulk with splat(mode 2) per bloom so it costs nothing per pixel and works as expanding discs on panels. Delete this file.

name: Nyan Lights
concept: Nyan Cat pixel art on a 16x16 canvas: pop-tart with frosting and sprinkles, gray cat head, bobbing rainbow, two-frame GIF wiggle.
visual_verdict: Recognisable pop-tart and gray cat, but the rainbow is drawn on the RIGHT, sitting on top of/behind the cat's head instead of trailing behind the tart, so the composition reads wrong; static apart from the 1-px jiggle.
perf_smell: none (fillCanvas, rebuilt only on change)
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: this is a two-frame animated picture — should be an animated .sprite, with the scrolling rainbow trail and twinkling stars as scene layers
cleanroom_quality: Fixed the serpentine hardcoding well, but the art placement is wrong (rainbow in front of the cat) and the cat is a tiny gray block.
action_notes: Redraw as a proper animated nyan .sprite (rainbow trailing left of the tart, legs cycling) and ship a 'Nyan' scene: sprite flying across a starfield with a scrolling rainbow trail. Delete the pattern.

name: Oasis
concept: Pacifica-style night ocean: four wave trains in both directions through a sin^4 crest LUT, crests whitening and hue-shifting.
technique: per-pixel LUT sum of 4 wave trains
visual_verdict: Waterfall is a green lattice of crossing diagonals with pale-yellow crest knots — reads green/lime, not the aqua/teal night ocean the spec describes (hue - bri*depth drags it toward green), and one visible discontinuity line.
perf_smell: 4x (mod + frac + LUT) per pixel — 0.42 ms, heavy for a 1D wave sum
cleanroom_quality: Mechanically faithful (reference-length normalization, LUT, breathing) but misses the look: the colour drifts green and four of five sliders are bare 0..1 dials.
action_notes: Two Pacifica takes is one too many; fold its bidirectional wave trains and whitecap threshold into ocean.js as the strip mode, delete this file.

name: Ocean
concept: Pacifica-spirited ocean: three scrolling wave layers summed through a deep-navy-to-foam palette, with a slow set-wave swell and whitecaps where crests coincide.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall: deep blue water with drifting diagonal foam glints — moody and pretty; on the grid it is index-only so just horizontal blue streaks per row with occasional foam lines.
perf_smell: none on strips; on 2D it wastes the panel (1D index math)
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Survivor of the ocean pair: add controls (swell speed, wave scale, foam amount, palette: night/tropical/stormy), absorb oasis's bidirectional trains, and add a real render2D (top-down caustic water via simplex3/fillNoise3D through the same palette, or side-view waves with depth) so panels get an ocean too.

name: opposites
concept: Two counter-travelling swells and a third wave warped by their sum multiply into sparse liquid blobs, coloured from two near-complementary hue clusters that drift round the wheel.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall shows soft lens-shaped blobs with rainbow-fringed rims and a green core on black — organic and genuinely different from the scroller crowd.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful and nicely controlled (real-unit cycle, ratio, spread %, glow %, mirror); the fringe banding comes from the hard hue fold.
action_notes: Minor: smooth the hue fold boundary to remove the rainbow fringing on blob rims, and add a 2D form (p = x, a second swell pair along y) so it is not a row-striped strip on panels.

name: Orv - Christmas Tree
concept: A drawn Christmas tree scene — green triangle, topper, garland, rainbow ornaments, brown ground, slate night sky — with drifting particles twinkling as tree lights and sky stars.
visual_verdict: Recognisable but crude: flat green triangle, an oversized yellow block 'topper' sitting inside the tree below a green tip, diagonal rainbow ornament speckle, and the 'stars' in the sky render as dark gray smudges rather than lights.
perf_smell: per-pixel loop over all star particles for every sky pixel (starLight) — 0.52 ms for a mostly static picture
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: a static picture with twinkle — tree as a .sprite, a sky colour wash, and a twinkle/sparkle pattern layer composed in a scene
cleanroom_quality: Follows the spec's layout, but the art is weak (topper block, index-speckle ornaments) and the sky-star rendering reads as dark smudges.
action_notes: Ship a 'Christmas Tree' scene: hand-drawn tree .sprite (proper star topper, ornament pixels), night-sky wash, a sparkle pattern layer masked to the tree for lights and a slow twinkly-stars layer for the sky, plus optional falling-snow layer. Delete the pattern.

name: Palette Fire 2D
concept: Fractal-noise fire: 3-octave perlinFbm scrolled over time, biased by height, through a black-red-orange-yellow-white palette.
visual_verdict: Rich, nicely coloured fire texture — but UPSIDE DOWN: the hot white-yellow band is at the top of the panel and it fades to black at the bottom, so it reads as a burning ceiling.
perf_smell: perlinFbm (3 octaves) per pixel; fillNoise3D rows / a small noise canvas upsampled would be far cheaper
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Bug: y=0 is the top, so 'heat + 0.9 - y*1.4' puts the base at the top — flip to (1 - y). Its palette+fbm approach is the cleanest of the noise-fire family; make it the core of the single surviving noise fire (perlin-fire) with wind/tunnel as controls, then delete this file.

name: Pendulum Wave
concept: Physics-classroom pendulum wave: one pendulum per pixel with graduated periods so the row drifts from unison into travelling waves, chaos and back to unison every 24 s.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall shows a lovely magenta/blue moire fan that tightens over time; on the grid it is index-based so pure aliasing hatching — and with one pendulum per pixel, long strips (300 px) will alias badly too.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Great concept, wrong rendering: on 2D draw one pendulum per column as a glowing bob (splat) swinging along y with a faint trail (fade) — the iconic look; on a strip group pixels into N pendulums (control, default ~15-24) so frequencies stay visible. Add controls: cycle seconds, pendulum count, palette.

name: Performance test framework
concept: Developer benchmark harness timing overhead/control/experiment functions and exporting a speedup ratio; a progress-bar readout was bolted on so the tile is not black.
visual_verdict: Red, green and blue progress bars filling the strip in turn — a status readout, not a pattern.
perf_smell: n/a (deliberately burns CPU)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful developer utility; frame-delta timing is meaningless as a micro-benchmark on Luxel (tools/opbench.mjs and builtinbench.mjs are the real instruments).
action_notes: Test scaffolding; Luxel has proper benchmark tools. Remove from the library (and from verify fixups nonVisual).

name: Perlin fire
concept: A base-anchored 2D fire: vertically stretched turbulence thresholded against a tapering fuel ramp makes licking tongues over a glowing ember bed, with sway, breathing and drifting embers through a black-red-orange-yellow-white palette; 1D fallback as a flame column.
visual_verdict: Convincing flame column rooted at the bottom with white-hot base, orange tongues and occasional rising sparks; a bit grainy/pixel-noisy at 32x32 and fairly narrow, but clearly the best fire in this range.
perf_smell: perlinTurbulence(4 octaves) + perlin + 3 pow per pixel — 0.59 ms at 1024 px, will be ~38 ms at 16384 px
cleanroom_quality: Explicitly forked from the original's four-noise demo (Jeremy, 2026-09-01) into a purpose-built flame with real-unit controls; delivers well.
action_notes: Survivor of the noise-fire family: add a Wind dial (absorb perlin-fire-wind's lean model verbatim) and a palette selector (classic/blue/green, absorbing palette-fire-2d's simple palette); perf — compute the turbulence on a coarse canvas (e.g. 24x32 via fillNoise3D/stencil per octave or a beforeRender loop) and paintCanvas-upsample, replace pow(...,0.75/0.85) with squares, which should cut cost several-fold on the 64x64.

name: perlin fire wind
concept: The same flame model as perlin-fire, leaned by a gusting, slowly reversing wind weighted by height; embers carried further than the flame.
visual_verdict: Frame-for-frame nearly indistinguishable from perlin-fire on the sheet — the wind lean is too subtle to see in 8 samples.
perf_smell: same as perlin-fire plus pow(hb,1.4) per pixel — 0.65 ms
cleanroom_quality: Forked deliberately to match perlin-fire plus wind; the code is perlin-fire copied with one extra function.
action_notes: Move the lean()/gust model into perlin-fire behind a Wind % dial (default 0 there, so perlin-fire's look is unchanged) and delete this file; consider a stronger default lean so wind is actually visible.

name: perlin fire wind tunnel
concept: Fractal-noise flame twisted into a vortex around the panel centre (rotation inversely proportional to radius) with a wind wobble; four noise flavours by mode.
visual_verdict: A sepia/tan spiral whirlpool — striking shape, but it reads as coffee swirl, not fire (single-hue hsv with bleaching, no red/orange ramp), and some frames go almost fully dark.
perf_smell: hypot + sin + cos + up to 3-octave noise per pixel (0.35 ms)
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the vortex twist, but all five controls are bare 0..1 dials (mode = floor(v*3.999) with step 0.05), the default hue makes it brown, and the dark frames suggest the cubic brightness curve crushes too much.
action_notes: Keep the vortex-twist idea as 'Fire Vortex' (or fold into swirlpool-2d as a fire palette): use the perlin-fire palette via paint(), a mode selector with step=1, real-unit controls (twist, revolution seconds, stream speed), and compute the twist with a precomputed per-pixel angle/radius only once (or sample a noise canvas) instead of hypot+sin+cos every frame.

name: Perlin/Simplex Noise 1D
concept: The strip as a profile slice through a noise landscape; coloured stripes sweep along equal-altitude contours (narrow on steep terrain, wide on flat), with optional panning and bass lurches.
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows regular wavy red/green/blue stripes on black — tidy but feels like a test card; the terrain-steepness effect is subtle.
perf_smell: full-strip noise rebuild every frame when Motion > 0 (array(pixelCount))
cleanroom_quality: Faithful, but 11 controls, nearly all bare 0..1 dials, including booleans as sliders and a debug 'Show Progress' overlay.
action_notes: One 'Topo Contours' pattern for strips and panels: the 1D path is just the 2D field sampled along a line. Drop Show Progress / X Offset / Perlin-or-Simplex dials, keep stripes, speed, scale, palette, bass kick.

name: Perlin/Simplex Noise 2D
concept: Animated topographic map: a cached 16x16 noise heightfield with coloured contour stripes sweeping from low to high ground, optional camera orbit and bass-driven lurches.
visual_verdict: BROKEN on the sheet: every frame is random red/cyan/green confetti at cell resolution — no contours, no smoothness, nothing resembling a topographic map.
perf_smell: 16x16 canvas recomputed every frame while panning (cheap), but nearest-cell lookup with hardcoded 15.99/16 indexing instead of canvasGet/fillCanvas
cleanroom_quality: Spec idea (animated contour map) is good, but the port renders as noise — likely the contour stripes alias at 16x16 nearest sampling (or the fractional seed/zoom), and all 12 controls are bare 0..1 dials.
action_notes: Rebuild as 'Topo Contours': fillNoise3D into a ~32x32 canvas with a slow z drift, bilinear sample (canvasGet or render2D with smooth contour lines via triangle + smoothstep anti-aliasing), OKLCH stripe hues; 1D strips sample a line through the same field (absorbs perlin-simplex-noise-1d). Real-unit controls: stripes count, flow seconds, terrain scale, palette, bass kick threshold.

name: Pew-Pew-Pew!
concept: A volley of neon laser bolts (pink-to-blue palette) firing down the strip at random speeds with fast-fading trails over a faint red ambient, plus a whole-strip 'blue lightning' flash whenever a bolt relaunches.
visual_verdict: Rows of short red streaks with occasional whole-frame blue wash; the pink/violet/blue bolt palette never shows because the default blue-lightning quirk replaces every pixel's blue with pixel 0's, so bolts read plain red.
perf_smell: 5x array(pixelCount) (r/g/b trails + two constant ambient arrays added and subtracted each frame) — renderBulk fade()+fillRange per bolt needs none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the original including its accidental blue-channel quirk, which is on by default and ruins the palette; good real-unit controls otherwise.
action_notes: The surviving comet/meteor pattern gains a 'laser bolts' style (short hard heads, per-bolt random speed, neon palette) and an optional launch-flash toggle defaulting OFF; implement on renderBulk with fade(k) and fillRange for swept pixels, no buffers.

name: pixelClock
concept: Analog clock for a strip or LED ring: blue seconds block, green minute block and a wider red hour block over a dim face.
visual_verdict: With the host clock at 00:00, a blue and a red block sit at the start of a dim gray strip, static apart from the per-second step — functional, not pretty.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful with the proportional-region fix from the spec and sensible colour pickers / 24 h / reverse toggles.
action_notes: Make it the ring-clock: smooth sweeping hands with soft anti-aliased edges (sub-pixel position from clockSecond + fraction), optional 12-o'clock and 5-minute tick marks, hour hand interpolating across the hour; on 2D panels hand off to an analog-clock scene/2D clock instead of striping rows.

name: Polar mapping helper 2D / 3D
concept: Diagnostic for polar/spherical maps: cycles radar sweep, axes+shell, index rainbow and octant modes, with an index chase, RGB ID blink on pixel 0 and a red pulse on the last pixel.
visual_verdict: On a Cartesian 32x32 it is horizontal red lines stepping down, then green/orange crosshair bars — a calibration screen.
perf_smell: function-array dispatch per pixel
cleanroom_quality: Faithful diagnostic, only meaningful on a polar-normalized map.
action_notes: Mapping diagnostics belong in the web UI's mapper (identify/test modes), not the shipped pattern library.

name: policeLights
concept: Emergency flasher: alternating 10-px red and blue-violet blocks hard-swapping five times a second.
visual_verdict: A rigid red/blue checkerboard flicker — crude, garish and nothing like a real light bar; strobe-y at 5 Hz.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to a trivial original; block size and rate remain hardcoded though the spec suggests exposing them.
action_notes: If kept, make it a real emergency light bar: left half red / right half blue with authentic multi-flash strobe sequences (quad-flash, alternating, sweep/rotator modes, white takedown flash) and a mode selector; otherwise delete. Mind photosensitivity — keep flash rates sane.

name: portal
concept: Pulses born near the strip midpoint widen and decay, summed into an intensity field mapped through a banded fire-portal gradient (thin red/orange bands, then through black into an indigo core).
technique: pulse pool into array(pixelCount) + hand-rolled 12-stop gradient
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall shows striking nested red contour rings around dark indigo domes — genuinely unusual; on the grid it is index rows only.
perf_smell: hand-rolled 12-stop gradient search per pixel plus mix() x3 and an array(pixelCount) accumulator — 0.51 ms
cleanroom_quality: Implements the intended design (full pool scan) and the banded palette well; no controls at all.
action_notes: Survivor of the pulse-pool trio (absorbs novas and scrolls as palette presets): install the banded gradient once with setPalette and use paint() (native, no per-pixel stop search); on 2D make it a real portal with rings expanding from the centre, with controls for pulse interval, lifetime, spread and palette (fire portal / embers / bioluminescent / void).

name: Post-Process Chain
concept: Teaching demo: seven hard single-pixel sparks on black, softened entirely by setOutputPalette/setBlur/setGlow/setGamma, one slider per stage.
visual_verdict: Dim indigo/magenta crossing diagonal lines on near-black; the softening is visible but the result is murky and low-energy.
perf_smell: per pixel loop over all 7 sparks (renderBulk clear()+setPixel x7 would be trivial)
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: A feature demo, not content, and its four 0..1 sliders duplicate what the post chain docs explain; move the snippet into docs/lang.md's post-process section. The 'sparks + glow' look is better delivered by a real pattern that uses setGlow (e.g. the comet/meteor survivor).

name: quiet blinkfade
concept: Sparse calm single-colour twinkle: pixels light at a random modest brightness, fade within a second and stay dark for seconds; one scalar per pixel is brightness and dead-timer.
visual_verdict: Almost black: a handful of very faint purple single pixels — the cap of 0.5 squared means sparks peak at 25% brightness.
perf_smell: interpreted loop over array(pixelCount) every frame with random() respawns
cleanroom_quality: Faithful (single-scalar trick) with good real-unit controls; the original's own brightness cap makes it too dim to be worth a slot.
action_notes: Collapse the blink/twinkle family into one Twinkle pattern with density (dark dwell s), fade s, peak brightness, colour/spread and palette controls; this file's dark-dwell model becomes its 'quiet' low-density setting.

name: Radar 2D
concept: Phosphor-green radar scope: a sweeping beam with afterglow computed from 'time since the beam passed this angle', a bezel ring, and contacts that flare when painted and relocate every third sweep.
visual_verdict: Recognisable radar — thin green beam, faint bezel, glowing blips — but very dark overall: the afterglow wedge is barely visible, so most frames are a thin line and dots on black.
perf_smell: atan2 + hypot + pow per pixel plus dist/atan2/pow per blip per pixel — 0.71 ms, among the heaviest in range
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Rebuild on renderBulk using the persistent frame as the phosphor: fade(k) each frame, drawLine from centre to rim for the beam, splat for blips when the beam crosses them, a cached bezel ring — near-zero per-pixel cost and a brighter, longer afterglow. Add controls: sweep seconds, persistence, contact count, colour (green/amber).

name: radiant pulse 3
concept: Soft bands pulse in and out around the centre, morphing between concentric rings, radial beams and a rotating clover, all driven by one ~5-minute master clock so speed breathes and reverses.
visual_verdict: Green/yellow starburst of radial beams with an orange centre, softly shifting; attractive kaleidoscopic look though over 8 s it barely changes and stays in one hue family (the hue cycle is 5 minutes).
perf_smell: hypot + atan2 + sin per pixel (0.25 ms); a per-pixel angle/radius table would remove the trig
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec's morphing ring/beam/clover idea with sensible real-unit controls.
action_notes: Rename (e.g. 'Radiant Bloom'); cache radius and angle per pixel once (they never change) and shorten the default master cycle so more of the morph is visible within a minute; consider OKLCH for the pastel cores.

name: Rainbow Comet
concept: A whitish comet head bounces back and forth; its tail fades while smearing through neighbouring hues, and the stamped base hue drifts so each pass lays down a different part of the spectrum.
visual_verdict: On the grid it is index-space, so a pastel bar crawls row by row down the panel; on a strip a soft pastel comet — pleasant but washed-out (low saturation) and plain.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount) plus an interpreted per-pixel loop; frame persistence + fade() makes the tail for free
cleanroom_quality: Faithful (span stamping, sat curing, hue smear) but both controls are bare 0..1 dials.
action_notes: The bouncing (triangle) head and hue-smearing tail become a 'bounce' motion option of the surviving meteor/comet pattern; delete this file.

name: Rainbow Flag
concept: Six static stripes violet-blue-green-yellow-orange-red along the strip (reverse flag order).
visual_verdict: Six solid colour columns, static forever; on a panel it is vertical bars rather than a horizontal-striped flag.
perf_smell: per-pixel render for a static image
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: a static picture — a flag sprite, or one option of a waving-flag pattern
cleanroom_quality: Faithful (keeps the reversed order); nothing to judge beyond that.
action_notes: Turn us-flag-2d into a 'Waving Flag' pattern with a flag selector (US, Pride/rainbow in correct order, Progress, Trans, ...) and a cloth-ripple shading; strips show the stripes scrolling gently. Delete this file.

name: rainbow fonts
concept: A mirror-symmetric rainbow about the strip midpoint, its hue a double sine-fold of centre distance plus phase, so bands compress and expand as it animates.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall: symmetric rainbow chevrons that breathe; vivid and smooth but just another full-saturation rainbow scroller.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful, with the brightness fix and good real-unit controls; the name ('fonts') is meaningless.
action_notes: The consolidated Rainbow gains Mirror, Repeats and a 'warp' (double sine-fold) amount; delete this file.

name: Rainbow
concept: The canonical default: one full hue cycle along the strip, scrolling.
visual_verdict: Clean scrolling rainbow; on the grid it is horizontal row bands (index order), fine but flat.
perf_smell: per-pixel render where renderBulk fillGradient(t,1,1,t+1,1,1) is one native call
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Make this the single rainbow survivor: renderBulk fillGradient (axis 0 on strips, axis 1/2 or an angle on panels), controls for speed (s/cycle), repeats, direction, mirror, warp, saturation, and an OKLCH mode for even brightness. Absorbs rainbow-pinwheel, rainbow-fonts, rainbow-v2 and bulk-rainbow.

name: Rainbow Melt
concept: A mirrored rainbow slowly rotating while brightness churns in fluid nested-sine waves on two near-equal periods.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall: flowing, melting rainbow ribbons over black with good contrast — the most interesting of the rainbow family.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: n/a (curated original written from a prose description; controls are real-unit)
action_notes: Keep as the 'rainbow with motion in brightness' entry; could absorb marching-rainbow as a 'ripple' variant. Add a 2D form (c from radius or x) so panels do not get row stripes.

name: rainbow pinwheel
concept: A folded scrolling rainbow (hue = sine of time + position) that sweeps up and back instead of wrapping; reads as a pinwheel on a ring.
visual_verdict: Plain diagonal rainbow bands with a fold — visually indistinguishable from the stock rainbow at a glance.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to a trivial original; controls are real-unit. Despite the name there is no pinwheel on a 2D panel.
action_notes: 'Fold' becomes a toggle on the consolidated Rainbow; if a pinwheel is wanted, the Rainbow's 2D mode should offer an angular (atan2) gradient. Delete this file.

name: Rainbow rocket sparks
concept: A fiery rocket head (red-yellow, colours fixed to the strip so it 'sheds exhaust') loops toward the start trailed by a window of random white sparks; stateless traveling square waves.
visual_verdict: Waterfall: a thin orange/yellow dash travelling diagonally with a few white spark flecks behind — hard-edged and sparse, reads as a test chase rather than a rocket.
perf_smell: random() per pixel per frame
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to a minimal original; hard square-wave edges, no fade on sparks, no controls.
action_notes: Fold into one 'Rocket Launch' strip pattern built on rocket-by-tony-hampton (accelerating body, boost, sputtering exhaust sparks, optional burst at apex); this file's 'exhaust colours fixed to the strip' trick is the only idea worth keeping as an option.

name: Rainbow Smiley
concept: A static 16x16 pixel-art smiley: white face disc with the background and eye/mouth cutouts filled by an animated wiring-order rainbow.
visual_verdict: Cheerful, clearly readable white smiley on a cycling rainbow background; the rainbow is index-order so it bands by rows, and the image never moves.
perf_smell: none
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: a static picture over an animated fill — a smiley .sprite composited over the Rainbow pattern in a scene
cleanroom_quality: Faithful; the index-order rainbow means it looks different on serpentine vs HUB75 wiring.
action_notes: Add a smiley .sprite (maybe with a blink/wink frame) and an example scene: Rainbow layer (diagonal or radial) + keyed sprite on top, optionally bouncing. Delete the pattern.

name: Rainbow v2
concept: The scrolling rainbow with spread, speed, direction, saturation and brightness sliders.
visual_verdict: Standard scrolling rainbow diagonals — identical in look to rainbow.js.
perf_smell: per-pixel where fillGradient is one call
cleanroom_quality: Faithful, but carries a pattern-level Brightness slider (house rule: remove on sight), a Direction slider used as a toggle, and bare 0..1 dials.
action_notes: Its spread/speed/direction/saturation controls become real-unit controls on the consolidated Rainbow (no brightness control); delete this file.

name: Raindrops 2D
concept: Rain on a still pool from above: random drops spawn expanding circular ripples via the two-buffer wave recurrence over a mottled blue-green floor with drifting shimmer; crests foam toward white.
visual_verdict: Very dark teal panel where ripple rings are only faintly visible as dim circles and the odd bright splash pixel; the idea is right but at default it reads as near-black murk with blocky 2x2 cells.
perf_smell: none (well optimized: stencil2D, feedback, flat-pool skip)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful and much improved (fixed step, mirrored edges, real-unit controls), but REST brightness 0.3 squared = 9% leaves the pool far too dark, and nearest-sampled 16x16 is coarse on a 64x64 panel.
action_notes: Survivor of the water-ripple trio: raise the rest level / use a palette with a brighter floor, run the sim at 32x32 (cost is native bulk ops) and upsample smoothly, add caustic-style highlights, and absorb ripples-2d's injected-event splashes (tap to drop) and bulk-canvas-ripples-2d entirely.

name: Rainstorm
concept: Deep-blue rain: columns of short streaks each with their own stable speed/brightness, perspective-stretched, rotatable, plus noise-gated lightning blooming from the centre.
visual_verdict: Dim navy dashes in a few columns on black, static-looking; one frame shows a faint lavender lightning wash — underwhelming and dark.
perf_smell: 2x hypot + sin + hash per pixel (0.38 ms) to draw sparse streaks; particles via drawLine on renderBulk would be far cheaper
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: rain layer + lightning flash layer is a natural scene (rain pattern under a lightning/cloud pattern)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful; all four sliders are bare 0..1 dials (angle as 0..1 of a full turn), and the result is too dim to read as a storm.
action_notes: One storm pattern: thunderstorm gains a 2D path — rain as drawLine streak particles with wind angle (degrees) and fade() motion blur, lightning as a bright branching bolt + sky flash; or ship rain and lightning as separate patterns composed in a 'Storm' scene.

name: Reaction Diffusion 2D
concept: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion on a 16x16 canvas; spots and worms self-organize, reseeding when the culture dies.
visual_verdict: Most frames are a full-panel blocky magenta/black noise texture with no recognizable spots or worms, then a single blob, then a purple smear — 16x16 is too small for Gray-Scott and it reads as static noise.
perf_smell: hand-rolled per-cell Laplacian loop (two steps x 256 cells x ~25 ops) where stencil2D/arrayMix bulk ops exist
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: Reaction-diffusion is a showcase-grade idea on a 64x64 panel: run Gray-Scott at 48x48 or 64x64 with stencil2D + arrayAdd/feedback (native), several steps per frame, controls for feed/kill presets (spots, worms, mitosis, coral), bilinear upsample and a proper palette (paintCanvas). Seed with a pattern, not 3 dots.

name: Real World Lights
concept: One slider picks among 13 real-world light presets: candle, three incandescent whites, uranium glass, HPS/mercury/sodium lamps, fluorescents, grow light, UV, Cherenkov blue.
visual_verdict: Default candle preset: busy high-frequency orange/red vertical flecks across the whole strip — reads as fizzing static rather than candlelight (no coherent flame breathing).
perf_smell: 4 sin per pixel for the animated presets; solid presets still render per pixel (renderBulk fill)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the preset list; the preset dial is a bare 0..1 slider (floor(v*13)) instead of a step=1 mode selector, and the candle noise is spatially too fine.
action_notes: One 'White & Lamp Light' utility: Kelvin dial, follow-the-day toggle (from naturallightsync) and a preset selector (step=1) for these lamps; rebuild candle as a coherent low-frequency flicker (simplex over time, slight spatial falloff) and render solid presets with fill().

name: regenbogendrogen
concept: A mirrored psychedelic rainbow: centre-distance ramp folded through wave() twice around a time phase, so colour bands compress and stretch.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall: symmetric rainbow chevrons breathing outward — practically the same image as rainbow-fonts.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful; the algorithm is the same double sine-fold of centre distance as rainbow-fonts with a different offset.
action_notes: Same as rainbow-fonts: mirror + warp options on the consolidated Rainbow cover it; delete.

name: RGBclock 2D
concept: Analog clock with red second / green minute / blue hour hands as additive angular gradients, a white sub-second hand, four radial and four hand-drawing modes, optional breathing sharpness.
technique: per-pixel polar math with pow per hand
visual_verdict: Hard to read as a clock: dim green and blue arc fragments at the rim, a small red/yellow wedge near the centre, no face or ticks; the hands are blurry wedges.
perf_smell: atan2 + sqrt + 4x pow per pixel — 0.95 ms, the heaviest pattern in this range
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to a complex original, but all 8 controls are bare 0..1 dials (two of them 4-way mode selectors as 0..1 step 0.25), and the default mode produces an unreadable face.
action_notes: Merge with 2d-clock-with-hand-color-pickers into one Analog Clock: renderBulk drawLine hands (anti-aliased capsules, additive mode 1 keeps the RGB-overlap idea), tick marks and a face ring drawn once, smooth sweep; style selector step=1 (classic, RGB additive, rings). Cost becomes a few line draws instead of per-pixel pow.

name: RGBW Mapping Tester - HSV Version
concept: Whole strip cycles solid red, green, blue, then half-brightness white via hsv saturation 0 (to exercise an RGBW white channel).
visual_verdict: Solid full-panel red/green/blue/gray frames in sequence — a colour-order test card.
perf_smell: per-pixel render of a uniform colour (fill() would do)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful diagnostic.
action_notes: Colour-order testing belongs in the web UI's output/LED setup page (a 'test colours' button), not the library; delete both RGBW testers.

name: RGBW Mapping Tester
concept: Whole strip cycles solid red, green, blue, then 1/3-intensity white to verify LED colour order.
visual_verdict: Solid red, green, blue and gray full-panel frames — a test card.
perf_smell: per-pixel render of a uniform colour
cleanroom_quality: Faithful diagnostic.
action_notes: Same as the HSV version: move colour-order checking into the device setup UI; remove from the library.

name: RGB-XYZ 3D Sweep
concept: 3D-map axis diagnostic: a soft planar band sweeps red along X, green along Y, blue along Z, one second each.
visual_verdict: Red vertical bar, green horizontal bar, then a full blue frame (z is constant on a 2D map) — a calibration sweep.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful diagnostic.
action_notes: Axis verification belongs in the mapper UI (an 'axis sweep' preview); remove from the library.

name: Ripples 2D
concept: Rain on a pond: three expanding rings, each a pure function of distance from its drop point, repositioning as they fade; real drops arrive as injected events (tap the preview, API or MQTT).
visual_verdict: Crisp, bright cyan rings expanding and overlapping on deep navy — clean and readable, visually better than raindrops-2d at default.
perf_smell: dist() (sqrt) per pixel per ring (0.49 ms); renderBulk drawing rings needs a ring primitive, or a shared radius table
cleanroom_quality: n/a
action_notes: The merged water pattern should take this one's look as the visual target (bright crisp rings) and its readEvent tap-to-splash input, on raindrops-2d's wave-sim engine; consider a 'stylized rings' mode that is this exact algorithm.

name: Rocket by Tony Hampton
concept: Rocket launch on a strip: a bright body accelerates up from the ground, boosts after a delay and streaks off the top, spewing additive white-hot exhaust sparks that cool and flicker; trails linger.
visual_verdict: On the 32x32 grid (index order) it is sparse dim white/orange specks across a few rows; no strip sheet was produced, but the code is a real launch-with-exhaust sim that should read well on a vertical strip.
perf_smell: 3x array(pixelCount) channel buffers + hsv2rgb per spark (fine for strips; fade()+setPixel on the persistent frame would drop the buffers)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful physics; four sliders are bare 0..1 dials (flight time, size, delay, boost should be seconds/pixels/x) and the display name carries the original author's name.
action_notes: Rename to 'Rocket Launch' and make it the survivor of the rocket family (absorb firework-rocket-sparks and rainbow-rocket-sparks); real-unit controls; optional firework burst at apex; on 2D, launch rockets vertically with drawLine exhaust and splat sparks.

name: Rock sparks
concept: A three-mode medley (confetti dust, three sweeping searchlights, spinning zooming rainbow checkerboard) with dithered crossfades — and it drives GPIO 25 high from 9-11pm to switch a house-lights relay.
technique: per-pixel mode dispatch, atan2/sin per beam
visual_verdict: Frames jump from sparse red/green confetti to green/violet searchlight beams to a hard rainbow checkerboard — an incoherent medley; the searchlight segment is the only striking part.
perf_smell: 3x atan2 + 6 sin per pixel in searchlight mode, random() per pixel in confetti (0.64 ms)
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: a timed medley of three looks is a playlist/scene, not a pattern
cleanroom_quality: Faithful, including the house-relay digitalWrite on a hardcoded pin every frame — a hardware side effect that must not ship in a library pattern; mode-B dials are bare 0..1.
action_notes: Remove (the GPIO relay write is dangerous on arbitrary boards). Salvage the searchlight mode as its own new 'Searchlights' pattern (drawLine beams with additive mode on renderBulk, beam colour pickers, sweep speed) if wanted.

name: RYB colors
concept: A slowly rotating conic colour wheel, switchable between the HSV wheel and a painter's RYB wheel built by trilinear RYB-cube interpolation.
technique: per-pixel transform + atan2 + RYB trilinear blend
visual_verdict: Smooth rotating pinwheel of warm RYB hues (big red/yellow sectors, narrow green) — pleasant but it is just a spinning colour wheel.
perf_smell: atan2 + HSL sextant + 8-corner trilinear blend with smoothstep per pixel every frame — 1.22 ms, the slowest pattern in this range; the hue->RGB mapping is a 1D function that belongs in a precomputed palette
cleanroom_quality: Faithful and correct RYB conversion, but carries a pattern-level Brightness slider (house rule violation) and bare 0..1 dials.
action_notes: The RYB conversion is worth keeping as a palette: bake it once into a setPalette table (or an engine-level 'RYB hue' option) and offer it as a hue-wheel mode of the consolidated Rainbow, whose 2D mode includes a conic (angular) gradient; delete this file.

name: SaberDeploy Tutorial
concept: Tutorial: a solid red 'light saber blade' extends from index 0 on a button press/injected event and retracts on the next.
visual_verdict: A flat red fill that grows to the whole strip and then just sits there solid red — no blade character at all.
perf_smell: none
cleanroom_quality: Faithful tutorial with delta-time fix and event-driven trigger; speed slider is a bare 0..1 dial and the directive sits on the export line oddly.
action_notes: Turn it into a real 'Lightsaber' prop pattern: eased ignite/retract with a hot white core and coloured glow, hum shimmer (low-frequency noise on brightness), brighter tip, clash flash on injected events, blade colour picker, ignite time in seconds. Drop the tutorial framing.

name: Scanner
concept: Doubled KITT/Cylon scanner: two halves each with a bouncing lead dot and fading comet trail, optionally revealing a frozen double rainbow.
visual_verdict: Strip waterfall shows a crisp mirrored X/diamond lattice of rainbow comets bouncing in and out — clean, classic, and nicer than a single scanner.
perf_smell: array(pixelCount) with an interpreted decay loop each frame; renderBulk fade()+fillRange would need no buffer
cleanroom_quality: Faithful (gap fill, mirrored start, rainbow mode); three bare 0..1 sliders.
action_notes: One Scanner/KITT pattern: modes single, mirrored pair (this file), and bounce-in-halves; rainbow or picked colour; speed in sweeps/s and trail in px; built on renderBulk fade() + fillRange so there is no buffer.

name: Scary Pumpkin
concept: A jack-o'-lantern: round pumpkin filled with a swirling fbm 'fire tunnel' texture, green triangle eyes/nose and a crescent smile flashing erratically via a tan(cos(...)) chaos flicker.
visual_verdict: Clearly a jack-o'-lantern with a bright green face that flashes on and off; the body texture is a dim brown wood-grain swirl rather than a glowing orange pumpkin, so it reads more 'wooden ball' than lantern.
perf_smell: atan2 + cos + sin + 3-octave perlinFbm per pixel inside the disc (0.40 ms); the texture could be a fillNoise3D canvas sampled through a precomputed swirl
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes (optional): face as a keyed sprite over a disc-masked fire layer would make the face art editable
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the spec (SDF face, chaotic deterministic flicker, tunnel-warped noise); the brightness mapping (|n|*0.45+0.06) keeps the body far too dark.
action_notes: Brighten the body with a real pumpkin palette (deep orange ribs via a cos(angle*ribs) term, glowing interior), default face colour to candle-yellow with green as an option, add a stem, precompute per-pixel angle/radius once, and move the noise to a small canvas. Good seasonal showcase once it glows.

name: scrolling text marquee 2D
concept: Marquee: blocky 8x8 glyphs from a hand-built mini font scroll right-to-left on a 16x16 canvas; on a strip it becomes a POV light-painting column.
visual_verdict: Peach-coloured blocky letters reading 'HLLO?!' (no E glyph exists, so the greeting is misspelled) scroll across, with long blank stretches.
perf_smell: none, but hardcoded 16x16 canvas with 15.99 indexing instead of the engine's text builtins
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: scrolling text is exactly what the engine's drawText/text layers in scenes do — this should be a text-layer scene
cleanroom_quality: Reproduces the glyph-store/fetch demo machinery but with a 6-glyph font, so it cannot spell a real message; superseded by Luxel's native text support.
action_notes: Delete the pattern; ship a 'Marquee' example scene: a scrolling text layer (textSlot/API-settable message, real font) over a dim animated background. The POV strip mode can be dropped.

name: scrolls
concept: Bioluminescent sea-green mounds fade up at random spots, hold and sink; a pulse pool summed into a field mapped through a six-stop black-teal-aqua-deep-teal gradient; generations wipe every ~4 s.
technique: pulse pool into array(pixelCount) + hand-rolled gradient
visual_verdict: Waterfall shows mound silhouettes with bright green rims but dark navy interiors (the gradient peaks mid-scale, so full-strength cores go dark), plus hard blackout cuts every generation.
perf_smell: array(pixelCount) field + per-pixel gradient stop search (0.37 ms)
cleanroom_quality: Faithful to the generated original, quirks included (dark cores, generation wipe); no controls.
action_notes: Becomes the 'bioluminescent' palette preset of the merged Blooms/portal pattern, with the core-goes-dark gradient fixed (peak at the top) and the generation wipe removed.

name: Shimmer Crossfade 2D
concept: Framework demo cycling three sub-scenes (rotating white line, rainbow plasma, rotating checkerboard) with a per-pixel random-dither dissolve between them.
visual_verdict: A soft white bar rotating for several frames, a speckled dissolve, then a dim magenta/blue dot-plasma grid — three unrelated mediocre looks; the sparkly dissolve is the only interesting moment.
perf_smell: all three setups run every frame; random() per pixel
scene_or_sprite_candidate: yes: cycling between looks with a transition is a playlist/scene job
cleanroom_quality: Faithful framework port with good controls (dwell s, crossfade fraction, hold scene); the sub-scenes themselves are filler.
action_notes: Propose an engine feature instead: a 'dither dissolve' transition type for playlists/scene layer switching (per-pixel stochastic crossfade, eased) — that is the one idea here worth keeping.

name: Sierpinski Rainbow 2D
concept: The Sierpinski triangle from a single fixed-point bitwise AND of x and y, with nested-wave brightness ripples and a rotating rainbow hue.
visual_verdict: Clear self-similar triangular fractal in saturated, shifting rainbow blocks — eye-catching but garish and blocky at 32x32, with some frames dropping to sparse dots.
perf_smell: none (cheap)
cleanroom_quality: Delivers the clever AND trick with good real-unit controls.
action_notes: Make it move: an infinite zoom loop into the triangle (scale by 2 per cycle wraps seamlessly because the fractal is self-similar) would be a real showcase; tone the palette (OKLCH, limited hue range option) and consider merging xorcery-2d-3d's XOR field as a second 'bitwise' mode.

name: Single Color Picker - wide or spot
concept: Utility: one picked colour across the strip, either a wide wash or a tight spot at a chosen location via a sharpness exponent.
visual_verdict: A static violet glow peaking at mid-strip and fading to the ends — exactly what it claims, nothing moves.
perf_smell: pow() per pixel every frame for a static image
cleanroom_quality: Faithful; Sharpness and Location are bare 0..1 dials and the picker's V acts as a pattern-level brightness.
action_notes: Fold into the single lighting utility as its 'Solid colour' mode: colour picker plus an optional spotlight (location in %, width in % of strip, softness); render with renderBulk fill() when wide.

name: sinpulse 3D
concept: Classic rainbow plasma: sin/cos of x, y and z with two drifting phases and a breathing zoom; field cubed so glowing crests sit on dark valleys.
visual_verdict: Big soft rainbow blobs (rings of yellow/green/magenta) breathing in and out — vivid when lit, but several frames are almost entirely black because cubing then halving crushes the field.
perf_smell: 3 trig per pixel; x/y terms could be per-column/per-row tables
cleanroom_quality: Faithful with good real-unit controls; the /2 after cubing makes it too dark too often.
action_notes: Make it the consolidated 'Plasma' (works 1D/2D/3D): drop the extra /2 or use a palette, add a style selector (soft blobs, neon contours from matrix-2d-honeycomb, two-tone complementary from matrix-2-tone-pulse), precompute per-row/per-column trig for 2D panels.
